claims.text: Incorporating a MoS2-based solid-lubrication phase into a high-entropy alloy will produce an in situ tribofilm during sliding.
The in situ tribofilm will be self-healing.
The MoS2-based phase will reduce friction and wear over a broad temperature range.
The sliding interface will develop a continuous, adherent, MoS2-rich tribofilm.
MoS2 shears easily during sliding to form a lubricious film.
The MoS2-rich film reduces adhesive interactions at the sliding interface.
The MoS2-rich film diminishes local plastic deformation.
Re-deposition of MoS2 particles during continued sliding can repair the tribofilm.
Tribofilm self-repair sustains low friction and low wear.
MoS2-modified high-entropy alloys will have a significantly lower coefficient of friction than untreated alloys across the tested temperature range.
MoS2-modified high-entropy alloys will have a significantly lower wear rate than untreated alloys across the tested temperature range.
Untreated high-entropy alloys exhibit higher friction under equivalent sliding conditions because they lack a self-lubricating phase.
Untreated high-entropy alloys exhibit accelerated wear under equivalent sliding conditions because they lack a self-lubricating phase.
The benefit will persist only while the MoS2 phase remains structurally intact and resistant to oxidation.
Highly oxidative or thermally excessive environments may limit the performance of the MoS2 intervention.
